clue.text: Earn a penny once you've got trade, for example

parts.note: to earn something is to win it
D, from the Latin denarius, was the symbol for the old pre-decimal British penny

explanation.surface: Someone is told they can make a little money once they have learnt a trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trade' looks like a job, but here it is the trade wind, an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The trade winds are the steady tropical breezes that sailing ships relied on, one example of moving air.

clue.text: Fools entertain visiting Italian gentleman, standing on head

indicators.note: the whole is stood on its head, so its top letter goes to the bottom
the entertain word comes visiting, joining after the gentleman

parts.note: signor is the Italian title for a gentleman
to amuse is to entertain

explanation.surface: Clowns put on a show for an Italian gentleman by doing headstands.
explanation.walkthrough: SIGNOR + AMUSE gives SIGNORAMUSE; 'standing on head' moves the opening S to the foot of the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignoramuses are ignorant people, dunces or idiots.

clue.text: Old magistrates had vermicide sprayed

indicators.note: sprayed suggests the letters of vermicide are scattered and land in a new order

explanation.surface: Ancient officials had worm-killer sprayed about.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome the decemvirs were a board of ten men holding official power, as when they drew up the Twelve Tables.

clue.text: Work with seabound vessel in noted surfing location

parts.note: a book is a literary work

indicators.note: in places the vessel word inside the sea word

parts.note: read as sea bound: the Med, short for the Mediterranean Sea, is bound round the vessel
Noah's ark is the classic crossword vessel

explanation.surface: Someone writes about a ship heading out to sea from a famous surfing beach.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'seabound' into sea (MED) bound round the vessel. 'surfing location' suggests a beach, but it means a web page whose address you have noted in a browser.
explanation.definitionFit: Saving a web page's address in a browser records where you were surfing so you can return.

clue.text: On cycling trip one's replaced good ladieswear

indicators.note: the good letter is swapped out and the one's letters put in its place

parts.note: out on a bike ride you are biking
one is I in Roman numerals, with its 's giving S

explanation.surface: Someone on a cycling holiday finds a good outfit has been swapped.
explanation.walkthrough: In 'one's replaced good' the IS takes the place of the G at the end of BIKING.
explanation.definitionFit: These are two-piece swimsuits worn by women on the beach.

clue.text: If no payment, real trouble for house with vacancy

indicators.note: trouble suggests the letters of If no payment, real are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A landlord warns that unpaid rent means real trouble for a house with an empty room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house with vacancy' looks like a property with a room to let; it is a household missing one of its two parents.
explanation.definitionFit: A household headed by a lone mother or father has one parent's place unfilled.

clue.text: Core time in office?

parts.note: the core of something is its middle, or mid
a term is a fixed period in office

explanation.surface: Someone asks about the central part of a politician's spell in power.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the meaning, as in the US midterm elections held halfway through a presidency.
explanation.definitionFit: The halfway point of a period of office, as in midterm elections, is the central part of that spell.

clue.text: State position for returning missile

parts.note: KY is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Kentucky
the lie of something is its position, as the lie of a golf ball

explanation.surface: Someone asks where to stand to catch a thrown weapon coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: A kylie is an Australian Aboriginal word for a boomerang.
explanation.definitionFit: This Australian word names the boomerang, the curved throwing stick that flies back.

clue.text: Butcher's type of art, they say

indicators.note: they say tells us the word for a type of art is heard spoken, not seen written

parts.note: deco is short for Art Deco, the 1920s and 1930s decorative style

explanation.surface: A butcher's shop is said to be a kind of art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butcher's' is British rhyming slang: butcher's hook means look. Dekko is British slang for a quick look.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang for taking a glance at something.

clue.text: Blow first of kisses to miss with curvy legs

parts.note: a knock is a blow

indicators.note: first of asks for the opening letter of the word kisses

parts.note: to miss someone is to need or want them back

explanation.surface: Someone blows a kiss to a girl they miss, admiring her shapely legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Being knock-kneed means the legs bend inwards so the knees touch, a curve in the limbs.

clue.text: Cut end off shaving stick

indicators.note: the instruction to cut the end off asks for the last letter of the shaving word to be dropped

parts.note: a flake is a thin shaving, as of chocolate or wood

explanation.surface: A man trims the end off his shaving stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaving stick' looks like a bar of shaving soap; 'stick' is the definition, in the sense of harsh criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal terms for heavy criticism, as in taking stick or taking a lot of hostile comment.

clue.text: Harry Brown's come over strange

indicators.note: the brown word has come over, or covered, the strange word, so it goes round it

parts.note: tan is a brown colour; the 's here stands for has
rum is old British slang for strange or odd

explanation.surface: Someone notices that a man called Harry Brown has started acting oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry is not a first name to pair with Brown but the definition: Harry S. Truman, US President 1945-53.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry was the first name of the American president who succeeded Roosevelt in 1945.

clue.text: One rescued from firing has retired and gone off

parts.note: someone who has retired for the night is in bed, so abed

indicators.note: off here means gone bad or awry, signalling the letters of gone are rearranged

explanation.surface: An employee saved from the sack has retired and gone away anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firing' looks like dismissal from a job; it means the fiery furnace of the Book of Daniel, from which this man was saved with Shadrach and Meshach.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Daniel he is one of three young Jews delivered unharmed from Nebuchadnezzar's blazing furnace.

clue.text: One making hollow bargain over drug with urchin

indicators.note: over means placed above in a down clue, so the bargain sits above the drug

parts.note: a gutter is one who guts, emptying out a fish or carcass
a snip is a bargain, something cheap
E is short for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone haggling over drugs with a street kid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One making hollow' sounds like a hollow promise; it is someone who guts a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A guttersnipe is a ragged child of the streets, a scruffy young waif.

clue.text: Armed band clear out from borders

indicators.note: the letters at the borders, the first and last, are taken out of the word for clear

parts.note: limpid means clear, as of water

explanation.surface: Militia are told to get out of the frontier regions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clear out' reads as one phrase meaning leave; split it, so 'clear' is the synonym and 'out from borders' the deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: An impi is a regiment of Zulu warriors, an armed body of fighting men.

clue.text: Chandler's material once provided by crime spate

indicators.note: the letters of crime spate supply, or provide, the answer once they are reordered

explanation.surface: A novelist's plots were once supplied by a run of real crimes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chandler' suggests Raymond Chandler and his crime novels, fitting 'crime spate'; it means a candle-maker.
explanation.definitionFit: This waxy substance from the head of the sperm whale was formerly used to make fine candles.

clue.text: Joining study on illness at hospital department

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn by heart
flu is a common illness, short for influenza
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: A student revises up on an illness while starting work in a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Confluent means flowing together, as two rivers merge into one stream.

clue.text: For Asian native skills one falls back on ace

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the reversed run follows the ace letter

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards

indicators.note: back tells us to read the run skills, one, falls from right to left

parts.note: arts are skills
I is the Roman numeral one
dips are falls or drops

explanation.surface: An Asian native's skills give way when facing an ace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' is a link. 'Asian native' sounds like a person; it is a plant. 'back' applies to the whole run of skills, one, falls, and 'on' puts that run after the ace.
explanation.definitionFit: This hardy houseplant is native to eastern Asia, especially China and Japan.

clue.text: In one visit, keys drop in glacier

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: In at the start tells us the keys go inside the one-and-visit pieces

parts.note: to call is to pay a visit
E and F are musical keys

explanation.surface: During a single visit someone drops their keys into a crevasse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drop' looks like a verb; it is a noun, a steep fall in a glacier's surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An icefall is the steep, broken section of a glacier where it flows over a sharp descent, like a frozen waterfall.

clue.text: A different girl?

parts.note: read as asking for a word meaning one more or a further one, as in a different girl entirely; the question mark signals the playful reading

explanation.walkthrough: The word means a different one, and it also ends in HER, a nod to the girl.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means one more of the same kind or a different one, as in try again with a new girlfriend.

clue.text: Back in pre-teens regularly missed vegetable

indicators.note: Back tells us to read the surviving letters from right to left
every other letter of pre-teens is missed out, leaving the alternate ones

explanation.surface: Children under thirteen regularly skip their vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: Missing R, T, E, S from PRETEENS leaves PEEN, which 'Back' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Neep is the Scots word for a turnip or swede, a root vegetable eaten with haggis.

clue.text: Phrases unjoined, and as yet unfamiliar

indicators.note: unfamiliar suggests the letters of and as yet appear in a strange new order

explanation.surface: Someone notes that the phrases have not been linked and are still new to them.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'and' that a joined phrase would need is itself part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: In rhetoric an asyndeton is a construction that leaves out the conjunctions, so its plural describes such phrases.

clue.text: First of autumn leaves in stacks

annotationWithheld.why: First of autumn leaves in stacks (1,4): A from 'First of autumn' and 'in stacks' = A GOGO are clear, but no standard sense of 'leaves' gives GOGO; the clue looks mis-set or misread and no source found
annotationWithheld.clue: First of autumn leaves in stacks

clue.text: Brute's expression of delight

explanation.surface: A thug shouts with joy.
explanation.walkthrough: Swift's Yahoos in Gulliver's Travels are coarse brutish humans, which gave the word its sense of a lout.
explanation.definitionFit: A yahoo is a coarse, boorish lout, and the same word is a whoop of joy, like yippee.

clue.text: Russian division missing referee's report?

explanation.surface: A Russian league game proceeds without the referee filing a report.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is the exclamation 'Oh, blast!' that an official might let out on missing an incident.
explanation.definitionFit: An oblast is an administrative region of Russia; Oh, blast is the cry of annoyance from someone who has just missed something.

clue.text: Stand behind one aiming to put points on board

definitions.text: Stand behind one aiming to put points on board

parts.words: Stand behind one aiming to put points on board
parts.note: read as the marked line in a pub that a darts player must stand behind when throwing to score on the dartboard

explanation.surface: Someone backs a hopeful trying to get points on the scoreboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand behind' reads as support a contender; it is literal, a line on the floor in darts.
explanation.definitionFit: The oche is the line behind which a darts player stands when throwing at the dartboard to score.

clue.text: I abandon heart of subject in semi-coherent summing up maybe

indicators.note: the I and shortened subject go in the semi-coherent piece

parts.note: articulate means coherent; semi takes half of it, the first five letters

indicators.note: the central letter of the word for subject is abandoned

parts.note: a theme is a subject, as of an essay

explanation.surface: A speaker admits to dropping the core of their topic in a muddled summing-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summing up' looks like a speech's conclusion; it means adding up figures. THEME loses its middle E to give THME.
explanation.definitionFit: Adding up numbers is a typical calculation, one of the basic operations of elementary mathematics.

clue.text: Belt tucked in round hen, say, as protection from sun

indicators.note: the belt word is tucked in between the round letter and the hen

parts.note: O is round in shape
a hen kept for eggs is a layer
a zone is a belt or band of territory

explanation.surface: A belt is fastened around a hen to shield it from the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: This band of the upper atmosphere absorbs most of the ultraviolet radiation from the sun.

clue.text: Tramp about to shelter in hollow tree-trunk

indicators.note: the word for about takes shelter in the emptied tree-trunk
hollow means the inside of tree-trunk is removed, leaving its first and last letters

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A vagrant is about to take shelter inside a hollow tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tramp' looks like a vagrant, which fits the scene; it is a verb, to hike a long way.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to walk a long, wearying distance, as on a long hike.
